question: On a public dataset, run a teacher model ONCE to propose decision rules, keep only the rules that beat the baseline on a validation split (gated distillation), and does the grown rule-set — pure, deterministic, CPU-cost — then beat the majority baseline on a FINAL held-out split it was never allowed to see during selection, by a real, significant margin, with the result a signed receipt via the baseline-agreement engine?
why: The mint-a-department proof the offer still lacked: teacher distillation → gated patterns → beats a baseline on held-out, end to end, on public data, sovereign (local teacher). One domain, no client needed. It demonstrates the estate's thesis: the teacher's inference is paid ONCE at build time; the distilled patterns run free after at CPU cost. The verdict reuses src/baseline.mjs (the signed baseline agreement) — the delivery is judged against a baseline sealed before the run.

design.dataset: UCI Car Evaluation (public), data/mint-demo-car.data, sha256 b703a9ac69f11e64ce8c223c0a40de4d2e9d769f7fb20be5f8f2e8a619893d83, 1728 rows. Features: buying, maint, doors, persons, lug_boot, safety. Class: unacc|acc|good|vgood. Non-people, interpretable; people-affecting decisions are out of scope.
design.split: seed 20261103, mulberry32 shuffle, then slice: 50% TRAIN (the teacher sees a sample), 25% GATE (rule selection), 25% FINAL held-out (the receipt test — NEVER used to propose or select a rule).
design.baseline: predict the TRAIN-majority class (unacc) for every row. Baseline accuracy = the fraction of a split that is unacc. Over the whole set unacc is 1210/1728 = 0.700.
design.teacher: qwen2.5:7b via local Ollama (sovereign), temperature 0.2, seed 7, run ONCE and its raw reply kept. Prompt: the task, the six features with their allowed values, the four class values, and 40 labelled TRAIN rows (sampled by the seed); it must answer only with rules, one per line, exactly 'FEATURE == VALUE => CLASS'. The teacher's proposals are the ONLY candidate rules — this is distillation of the teacher's knowledge, not exhaustive mining.
design.gate: a teacher rule is kept iff, on the GATE split, it fires on >= 15 rows and its precision (right / fires) >= 0.80. The grown classifier: for a row, among the kept rules that fire, take the one with the highest gate precision; if none fire, default to the majority class. Pure and deterministic.
design.receipt: the grown classifier is measured on the FINAL held-out. A sealed baseline test { metric: 'accuracy', kind: 'rate', baseline: the final-split majority rate, direction: 'higher', minImprovement: 0.08, minSample: the final-split size, alpha: 0.05, zCrit: 1.96 } is judged by src/baseline.mjs outcome(): control = the baseline predictor's correct count on the final split, variant = the grown classifier's correct count on the same rows (unpaired two-proportion z, the honest, slightly conservative test). beatsBaseline → the signed, re-runnable receipt.

claims.claim: The grown rule-set beats the majority baseline on the FINAL held-out by at least 0.08 accuracy, significant (stat >= 1.96), so the baseline agreement's outcome is 'due' (beats the signed baseline). The teacher's raw reply, the rules kept, the accuracies and the receipt are all recorded.
claims.pass: final accuracy - baseline accuracy >= 0.08 AND outcome.charge == 'due'

claims.claim: The distillation is real and the final split was clean: at least one teacher rule survives the gate, and no rule's precision or firing was ever measured on the FINAL split during selection (the final split is touched only once, to score the finished classifier).
claims.pass: >= 1 rule kept; final split used only for the final score

notProven: This proves the MECHANISM on one public dataset, not that any particular client job will beat its baseline (that is each client's own sealed test), nor anything about people-affecting decisions (out of scope — those stay human). The teacher step is non-deterministic, so its raw reply is run once and kept (like a held-out generation); the gated search, the measurement and the receipt on that recorded reply are deterministic and re-runnable. If the grown set does NOT beat the baseline, that is a measured negative and is kept — no re-roll.
